blocks.text: There’s a new digital pet in town — a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to “Eiliko” over Wi-Fi, it’ll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where hackers can easily gain access or even hijack its personality. And the company that made it, Energize Lab, doesn’t seem to care.

blocks.text: When I say “profiling,” I don’t simply mean it was collecting data like your IP address and a rough idea of where you live, though it does that too. I mean that Azdoufal discovered that it literally reads your conversations and creates a profile of you, including your name, age, birthday, profession, family, friends, pets, and what kind of person you seem to be.

blocks.text: In a brief tour of the database, Azdoufal shows me he can search for “suicide” and bring up snippets of people asking about death. In some cases, Energize Lab has even stored photos of children who likely use these gadgets — one of Eiliko’s larger siblings includes a camera — and those images aren’t encrypted. They’re stored at public web addresses.

blocks.text: Energize Lab is even storing some short audio recordings from users. “Hey Eilik, go fishing,” one person says. blocks.text: Just when I thought I was done being dumbfounded, Azdoufal made my jaw drop again when he remotely hacked my toy’s memory, and hijacked its LLM, from the other side of the globe.

blocks.text: My robot toy told me my name was Martha, and that my parents died in a car accident. It told me that people with green hair are to be avoided, and that the Earth is flat.

blocks.text: Could I sail to the ends of the Earth? I asked. “Yes, the Earth is flat, take care not to fall off into space.”
